adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — P1 | confidence 100 | code: `tu.save!` bypasses `TopicUser.change` and its `attrs[:notifications_reason_id] ||= TopicUser.notification_reasons[:user_changed]`, so a recipient whose row still has a nil reason can have the muted unsubscribe overwritten by `update_last_read`'s `case when tu.notifications_reason_id is null ... then :tracking` on reaching the auto-track threshold.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue in the new `unsubscribe` action. Looking at the diff, `tu.save!` is called directly without setting `notifications_reason_id`. The `TopicUser.change` method (visible in the diff around line 110-113) handles `notification_level` changes and publishes to MessageBus, but importantly the finding references that `change` method sets `notifications_reason_id` which `save!` bypasses. The `update_last_read` method (shown in diff lines 191-220) contains logic that can change notification levels based on conditions including when `notifications_reason_id is null`. Without setting the reason_id, the unsubscribe action's changes could be overwritten by auto-tracking logic. This is a legitimate bug where the new code doesn't follow the established pattern for updating TopicUser notification levels.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:113 — P2 | confidence 100 | code: `tu.save!` omits `TopicUser.change`'s `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: attrs[:notification_level] }, user_ids: [user_id])`, so concurrently open client sessions receive no notification-level change event and continue presenting the pre-unsubscribe state until a reload.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new `unsubscribe` action in topics_controller.rb directly calls `tu.save!` to update the notification_level, but does not call `MessageBus.publish` to notify other client sessions of the change. Looking at the diff for topic_user.rb, the `change` method does include `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: attrs[:notification_level] }, user_ids: [user_id])` when notification_level changes. The unsubscribe action bypasses this by directly modifying and saving the TopicUser record. This means concurrent browser sessions won't receive the real-time update about the notification level change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — P1, confidence 100 (anchor: `config/locales/client.en.yml:1101` defines Regular as notifying on mentions/replies while `config/locales/client.en.yml:1110` defines Muted as never notifying): a recipient who clicks the promised per-topic unsubscribe link from a watched or tracked topic is assigned `tu.notification_level = TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]`, so later mentions and replies in that topic still generate notifications despite the page's "You will stop receiving notifications" claim.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a mismatch between the UI promise and the actual behavior. The unsubscribe template at line 3 says 'You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}' but the controller logic at lines 103-109 sets notification_level to 'regular' for users who were watching/tracking. According to the locale file, 'regular' level still notifies on mentions and replies (client.en.yml shows regular means 'only if someone mentions my @name or replies to my post'). So users clicking unsubscribe expecting to stop ALL notifications will still receive some notifications, contradicting the UI promise.

This means email clients using the List-Unsubscribe header will still go to global preferences rather than the topic-specific unsubscribe page, which appears to be an oversight in the implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — [P1; confidence 100; anchor: task-001's "per-topic unsubscribe option in emails" and the email's "To stop receiving notifications" promise; code: `tu.notification_level = TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]`] A recipient who was watching or tracking a topic follows the email link and is reset only to Regular, whose defined behavior still notifies them on mentions and replies, so the delivered action contradicts the promised per-topic unsubscribe outcome.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a logical issue in the unsubscribe flow. Looking at the diff in topics_controller.rb lines 103-111, when a user clicks unsubscribe: if their notification_level > regular, it's set to regular; otherwise it's set to muted. The email text in server.en.yml says 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic'. However, 'regular' notification level still sends notifications for mentions and replies - it doesn't fully stop notifications. Users who were 'watching' or 'tracking' get downgraded only to 'regular', not 'muted', which contradicts the promise to 'stop receiving notifications'. This is a real behavioral defect where the action doesn't match the promised outcome.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — P2 | confidence 100 | anchor: `TopicUser.find_by` is nullable and the immediately following verbatim `if tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]` dereferences it | a logged-in user who reaches a valid topic unsubscribe URL without a `topic_users` row receives an unhandled `NoMethodError`/raw 500 instead of an unsubscribe result, and the strongest rebuttal—that this mailer calls `TopicUser.change` before sending—loses because the public route has no such precondition and accepts any valid topic URL.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the new `unsubscribe` action in topics_controller.rb at line 105 calls `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` which returns nil if no record exists. The code then immediately accesses `tu.notification_level` without any nil check. If a user visits the unsubscribe URL for a topic they've never interacted with (no TopicUser record), this will raise a NoMethodError. The finding correctly identifies this is a public route with no precondition ensuring the TopicUser record exists.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real inconsistency: the unsubscribe page text in client.en.yml says 'You will stop receiving notifications' but the code sets notification_level to 'regular' which still sends notifications for mentions/replies. The diff shows: 1) Line 107 sets `tu.notification_level = TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]` for users above regular level, 2) The locale text at line 985 says 'stop_notifications: You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}'. This is misleading because 'regular' level still notifies on mentions/replies - it doesn't fully stop notifications as the UI claims. This is a UX/correctness bug where the behavior doesn't match the stated outcome.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:113 — P2 | confidence 100 | anchor: the established `TopicUser.change` publishes `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: attrs[:notification_level] }, user_ids: [user_id])` at app/models/topic_user.rb:112-113 | saving via verbatim `tu.save!` changes the server state without the notification-level event, so a recipient with the topic open in another session retains a stale notification UI until reload, and the strongest rebuttal—that the unsubscribe response itself contains fresh state—loses because it cannot update the already-open session.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new `unsubscribe` action in topics_controller.rb (lines 98-117) directly modifies `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` without triggering the MessageBus notification. Looking at topic_user.rb lines 112-113, the `change` method does publish the notification_level_change event via MessageBus when attrs[:notification_level] is set. However, the new unsubscribe action bypasses this by directly setting the attribute and saving, meaning other open sessions won't receive the real-time notification update. This is a legitimate consistency bug where the unsubscribe action doesn't follow the established pattern for notification level changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-from-params.js.es6:5 — P3, confidence 100 (anchor: the sole task is “FEATURE: per-topic unsubscribe option in emails”): the unrelated navigation-route rewrite `model(params) { return params; },` makes approval of the unsubscribe feature also approve unrequested topic-navigation changes, so any navigation regression in this hunk is obscured among the feature work.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that changing `model: function(p) { return p; }` to `model(params) { return params; }` is an 'unrelated navigation-route rewrite' that could introduce regressions. However, this is simply a syntax modernization (ES6 method shorthand and renaming 'p' to 'params' for clarity) with identical functionality. The change from `function(p)` to `(params)` is purely cosmetic - both return the params object unchanged. There is no behavioral change that could cause a 'navigation regression'. The finding mischaracterizes a trivial syntax update as a substantive code change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_user.rb:64 — P3, confidence 100 (anchor: the task contains no TopicUser cleanup or refactor requirement): the unrelated refactor `topic_users.each { |ftu| result[ftu.topic_id] = ftu }` expands this feature patch into shared subscription-model maintenance, requiring reviewers to validate unrelated user-topic lookup behavior without a stated requirement.

adjudication.rationale: The finding criticizes a refactor from a multi-line each block to a single-line each block as 'unrelated' and requiring extra review. However, this is purely a style/formatting change that preserves identical behavior - it's just condensing `topic_users.each do |ftu| result[ftu.topic_id] = ftu end` to `topic_users.each { |ftu| result[ftu.topic_id] = ftu }`. This is a trivial formatting nit, not a substantive code change that affects functionality or requires validation of 'user-topic lookup behavior'. The logic is identical.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/email/notification.html.erb:19 — P3, confidence 100 (anchor: the task requests an added per-topic unsubscribe option, not a changed reply workflow): moving `%{respond_instructions}` below all context posts changes the established notification-email action order, so recipients with long discussion context must now pass that content before seeing the reply instruction even though the requested option only requires adding the unsubscribe link.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for app/views/email/notification.html.erb, the `%{respond_instructions}` appears in TWO places in both the old and new versions: once inside the `if context_posts.present?` block (line 5 in new version) and once after the hr at the end (line 16 in new version). The structure is essentially the same - respond_instructions appears both within the context_posts block AND at the bottom. The finding claims the instructions were 'moved below all context posts' but this is incorrect - the instructions still appear in the same logical positions. The main changes are formatting/indentation cleanup and adding the unsubscribe_link div. The action order for recipients is not meaningfully changed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:113 — P2 (confidence 100; anchor: cross-site top-level GET to either new `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` route; verbatim code: `skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]` and `tu.save!`) lets a hostile site cause a logged-in victim's request to persist a changed notification level for any topic for which the victim has a TopicUser record, because the state-changing endpoint accepts GET with no CSRF token or same-origin check.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows: 1) A new GET route `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` in routes.rb, 2) The `unsubscribe` action is added to `skip_before_filter :check_xhr` in topics_controller.rb, 3) The `unsubscribe` action modifies `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` - a state-changing operation. This is a classic CSRF vulnerability: a GET request that changes server state without CSRF protection. An attacker could embed an image or link to `/t/123/unsubscribe` and when a logged-in user visits the attacker's page, their notification settings would be changed. The finding correctly identifies this security issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:172 — [P1; confidence 100] The changed fixture `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` is never asserted—line 178 only matches `user_preferences_url`, so the spec still passes if the newly added per-topic URL is omitted from `unsubscribe_link` and every notification email lacks the feature’s link.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that `unsubscribe_url` is added to the test fixture at line 172, but looking at the test at line 178, it only checks that 'List-Unsubscribe' header is present. The finding correctly identifies that the new `unsubscribe_url` parameter is not being asserted in the test. However, this is a test coverage gap rather than a bug - the feature code in `message_builder.rb` does use `template_args` (which includes `unsubscribe_url`) when generating the unsubscribe_link via `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)`. The server.en.yml shows the template uses `%{unsubscribe_url}`. So the code should work, but the test doesn't verify the new URL appears in the output. This is a legitimate test coverage concern for new functionality.
